notes: Read all targets, context and fifteen candidates. Restore U.S. and 2008 temporal scope, including the winter governing both forecasts without inventing exact winter dates. Add the omitted economy-wide harm. Normalize the energy-supply requirement as policy. The final rhetorical slogan duplicates the retained opposition to energy defeatism and adds no separate substantive claim.

claims.claim_text: In 2008, Americans are acutely aware of the U.S. energy crisis.
At the time of the 2008 platform, U.S. energy costs are rising rapidly.
At the time of the 2008 platform, U.S. food prices continue to rise.
Rising energy and food prices are hurting the entire U.S. economy at the time of the 2008 platform.
In the winter anticipated by the 2008 platform, U.S. families will spend on heating money that could otherwise have been saved for college.
In the winter anticipated by the 2008 platform, U.S. small businesses will spend on fuel money that could otherwise have covered employee health insurance.
U.S. dependence on foreign fossil fuels in 2008 threatens both U.S. national security and the economy.
U.S. dependence on foreign fossil fuels in 2008 could force drastic changes in Americans' way of life.
At the time of the 2008 platform, Americans transfer approximately $700 billion annually to OPEC.
The annual transfer of approximately $700 billion from Americans to OPEC described in 2008 helps finance terrorist operations.
The annual transfer of approximately $700 billion from Americans to OPEC described in 2008 provides little incentive for repressive regimes in the Middle East or Latin America to accept democracy.
Support for a strong U.S. energy supply because energy promotes prosperity and opportunity for every American.
